headline: Google is cutting free Gemini users down to its smallest model and taking Pro away from its five-dollar subscribers.
score_reason: Affects every free Gemini user, but a single outlet reports it and its own assessment is that the practical impact is small.
importance_line: Free users and $4.99 AI Plus subscribers lose access to Google's stronger Gemini models unless they pay $19.99 or more a month, a shift toward OpenAI's pay-for-the-best-model approach, though The Decoder itself notes most casual users will not notice which model they run.
summary: The Decoder reports that from October 2026 Google limits Gemini users without a subscription to its smallest model, Flash-Lite, while the $4.99-a-month AI Plus tier loses the Pro model and all three models require AI Pro at $19.99 or AI Ultra at $99.99 or more, according to Google's support page. The Decoder reads this as mirroring OpenAI's ChatGPT freemium model and as a possible step toward the larger, costlier Gemini 4 Argon, while judging the day-to-day impact small.
notes: Short article; tier details rest on Google's support page, impact judgement is The Decoder's own.
